reason: E1 and E2 support the general concept that small coherent precipitates can strengthen without degrading soft magnetic properties, but they do not provide specific evidence for MnNiSi-CoNiGe alloys, the claimed 30–50% strength increase, or the preservation of a magnetostructural transition and its large ΔS. The cited evidence is only loosely related to the key premises about this specific material system and the quantitative predictions.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates below ~15 nm can strengthen without pinning magnetic domain walls
Domain wall thickness in soft magnetic materials is ~50 nm to a few µm, so sub-15 nm precipitates do not interact with them
Precipitation strengthening can increase yield strength by 30–50% and improve ductility
The magnetostructural transition and associated large ΔS can be preserved if precipitates are small and coherent
A two-step heat treatment can produce uniformly distributed coherent nanoprecipitates <15 nm in MnNiSi-CoNiGe
